newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks open down after Dow falters.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks open down after Dow falters.

text.p: Australian shares opened slightly weaker on Wednesday, the market's early direction set by Wall Street which was hit by profit-taking and investor jitters ahead of U.S. third-quarter earnings reports.
At 10.15 a.m. (0015 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was down 2.7 points at 2,329.
The June share price index was one point weaker at 2,358 and at a 29-point premium to the underlying index.
Brokers said transport group Brambles Industries, which went ex-dividend, contributed to the market's early weakness. Brambles is paying a final dividend of 35 cents today.
"Most major issues have opened a few cents weaker but there doesn't seem to be much direction out there early," a dealer at a Sydney-based brokerage said.
The dealer said BHP and CRA were neutral early with a rally in the price of copper helping to stem further falls for major resource groups in the wake of the recent softness of base metal prices.
"The most positive sign for the market is the December SPI futures contract which is still holding onto a reasonable premium," the dealer said.
The shares of life office National Mutual remained very active following their strong debut on Tuesday. The group's stock was weaker in early trade at A$1.76, down from a close on Tuesday of A$1.80.
